question: Question linked to the image nº26 A 26-year-old man who presented erythematous-scaly plaques on the scalp, elbows, sacral region, periumbilical and knees for 7 years. He has followed different treatments (acitretin, methotrexate, cyclosporine, phototherapy) that have been only partially effective or have caused adverse effects. Which of the following drugs has an approved indication for our patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Erythematous-scaly plaques on the scalp, elbows, sacral region, periumbilical, and knees for 7 years" -> "Chronic plaque psoriasis likely" -> "Previous treatments with acitretin, methotrexate, cyclosporine, and phototherapy" -> "Partial effectiveness or adverse effects noted" -> "Consider biologic therapy" -> 70% CHAIN: "Biologic therapy considered" -> "Options include Abatacept, Ustekinumab, Leflunomide, Tocilizumab" -> "Evaluate approved indications for each drug" -> 80% CHAIN: "Abatacept" -> "Approved for rheumatoid arthritis, not psoriasis" -> "Unlikely to be indicated for the patient" -> 90% CHAIN: "Ustekinumab" -> "Approved for moderate to severe plaque psoriasis" -> "Likely indicated for the patient" -> 95% CHAIN: "Leflunomide" -> "Not typically used for psoriasis" -> "Unlikely to be indicated for the patient" -> 85% CHAIN: "Tocilizumab" -> "Not typically used for psoriasis" -> "Unlikely to be indicated for the patient" -> 70%
analysis: The patient described has a history of psoriasis with involvement of multiple body areas and has not responded well to conventional treatments. Ustekinumab is a biologic agent approved for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy. It targets specific proteins in the immune system that are involved in the development of psoriasis.
